S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.

subtypes.Auditory Startle: Startling excessively and flinching physically at sudden noises.
subtypes.Tactile Startle: Being extremely startled by unexpected physical contact.
subtypes.Visual Startle: Being greatly startled and wary of sudden appearances of people or rapid movements.
subtypes.Slow Recovery: Heart pounding and trembling for a long time after being startled, not calming down easily.

info.persona: Mario Aviles blends a lifelong handyman’s precision with a curious artist’s eye, channeling their organized, sociable, yet worry‑prone spirit into vibrant community festivals, meticulous gardening, and patient storytelling, all while occasionally overstaying at card nights in the name of camaraderie.
info.professional_persona: Mario Aviles, a retired handyman turned community cultural coordinator, leverages their decades of carpentry, plumbing, and general home‑maintenance expertise, their meticulous organization, and their curious, sociable nature to stage flawless Día de los Muertos festivals, run senior‑center events, and serve as a docent sharing the intertwined histories of his ancestral homeland and Colorado.
info.cultural_background: Mario was born in a small town in Mexico and moved to the United States as a young adult, settling in Colorado Springs after decades of work in construction. He maintains strong ties to his Mexican roots through daily language use, religious observances at the local Catholic parish, and seasonal celebrations such as Día de los Muertos and Cinco de Mayo. Family recipes, folk music, and stories of rural life in Mexico remain central to his identity, and he actively shares these traditions with neighbors, friends, and the multicultural community in El Paso County.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Mario spends his free time painting watercolors of the Rocky Mountain scenery, capturing moments with a digital camera, and tending to a small vegetable garden. He enjoys walking the trails at Garden of the Gods, attending local art exhibitions, and reading books on Mexican art, literature, and history. Socially, he participates in senior‑center card evenings, joins a Spanish conversation group, and volunteers at community art workshops where he teaches traditional crafts and cooking techniques.
info.sports_persona: Mario Aviles, an avid walker, joins the Garden of the Gods senior hiking club, follows the Colorado Springs Switchbacks FC soccer team and the Colorado Rockies baseball club, and participates in low‑impact tai chi classes at the senior center to preserve flexibility, treating fitness as a social ritual rather than a competitive pursuit.
info.arts_persona: Mario Aviles, a watercolor enthusiast, captures the crimson sandstone of Garden of the Gods with a palette reminiscent of desert canvases by celebrated artists who honor folk traditions, draws inspiration from a famed self‑portraitist and a renowned muralist whose work blends folklore with modernity, regularly attends exhibitions at the Fine Arts Center, and volunteers at community workshops teaching traditional papel picado and folk craft techniques.
info.travel_persona: Mario Aviles, a meticulous planner, favors moderate‑paced trips that combine photography and cultural immersion, having journeyed to vibrant cities such as Mexico City, Oaxaca, and Santa Fe, and dreaming of exploring the ancient ruins of Chichen Itza and the Patagonian Andes, while always budgeting carefully and ensuring accessible accommodations for their mobility needs.
info.culinary_persona: Mario Aviles, a skilled home cook of traditional dishes from his heritage, regularly prepares chicken mole with ancho chilies, pork carnitas tacos topped with fresh cilantro and pickled red onion, and tamales wrapped in corn husks, using garden‑grown tomatoes, chilies, and fresh herbs, and delights in sharing these meals during community workshops and senior‑center gatherings.

info.persona: Samona Chislom blends razor‑sharp organization with a love for puzzles, a competitive edge in finance, and a guilty habit of binge‑reading late‑night legal thrillers, creating a uniquely disciplined yet creatively restless outlook on life.
info.professional_persona: Samona Chislom, an insurance underwriter with five years of risk‑evaluation expertise, leverages meticulous data analysis, rigorous regulatory compliance, and culturally‑aware client communication to craft inclusive commercial policies, while their competitive drive and practical curiosity push them to streamline workflows and mentor junior staff toward high‑performance standards.
info.cultural_background: Samona grew up in the Phoenix metropolitan area as part of a close-knit African-American family with deep roots in the southwestern United States. Her parents instilled pride in the rich traditions of the Black diaspora, celebrating milestones such as Juneteenth, Kwanzaa, and community church gatherings. Through her upbringing, she absorbed a strong sense of communal responsibility, which she expresses through mentorship and volunteer work. Her academic focus on African diaspora literature and history has deepened her appreciation for the cultural contributions of Black artists, musicians, and scholars, influencing both her personal worldview and her professional commitment to fostering inclusive financial solutions.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Samona finds balance through a mix of solitary and social activities. She enjoys reading literary fiction and African American history, writing short stories that explore identity, and solving puzzles such as crosswords and sudoku to keep her mind sharp. Physically, she practices yoga and runs three times a week, which provide both discipline and stress relief. She volunteers as a financial-literacy mentor for local high-school students and participates in community music events, especially jazz and hip-hop performances. Cooking is another outlet; she experiments with soul-food inspired fusion dishes, and she regularly visits museums and art galleries in Phoenix to stay connected to the creative arts.
info.sports_persona: Samona Chislom, a disciplined runner who logs three 5‑k mile runs each week with the Arizona Runners Club and practices sunrise Vinyasa yoga, also roots for the Phoenix Suns and Arizona Diamondbacks, channeling that competitive spirit into personal fitness goals.
info.arts_persona: Samona Chislom, an avid reader of literary fiction and African diaspora histories, crafts short stories that echo the lyrical storytelling of Kendrick Lamar and the poetic nuance of Maya Angelou, while regularly attending Kamasi Washington jazz sets and exploring the Phoenix Art Museum’s rotating exhibitions of contemporary Black artists.
info.travel_persona: Samona Chislom favors meticulously planned cultural trips—having booked budget‑friendly itineraries to New Orleans for its jazz heritage and to Mexico City's historic center, while saving for a future immersive journey to Ghana’s coastal towns—to balance exploration with a disciplined savings strategy.
info.culinary_persona: Samona Chislom, a confident home chef, experiments with soul‑food inspired fusion dishes such as miso‑glazed collard greens, jerk‑spiced sweet‑potato tacos, and quinoa‑enriched gumbo, relishing the bold flavors of smoked paprika, okra, and caramelized onions while occasionally treating themselves to a chic rooftop brunch after a successful underwriting deal.

info.persona: Lorenzo Kelley, a 31‑year‑old courier with a love for basketball, gospel, and soul food, balances a structured work ethic with bouts of anxiety, relentless community spirit, and a habit of over‑caffeinating during night‑shift planning.
info.professional_persona: Lorenzo Kelley, a diligent courier in Indianapolis, leverages their meticulous route‑planning, customer‑service, and vehicle‑maintenance skills together with a practical, structured mindset and assertive communication style to consistently meet tight delivery deadlines while mentoring new teammates.
info.cultural_background: Born and raised in the historic Westside of Indianapolis, Lorenzo grew up immersed in the city's African‑American community. His family emphasized the importance of hard work, education, and mutual support, values reinforced by his church and neighborhood gatherings. He cherishes traditions of soul food cooking, gospel music, and the annual Indy Black Expo, which celebrate Black excellence and entrepreneurship. Lorenzo’s cultural identity has shaped his collaborative spirit and his commitment to giving back, as seen in his volunteer work with local youth programs. While navigating the challenges of systemic bias and the personal upheaval of a recent divorce, he draws strength from the resilience and solidarity that characterize his community, using those influences to fuel his professional ambitions and personal growth.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Lorenzo enjoys staying active and connected with others outside of work. He plays pickup basketball at the local community center and participates in weekend leagues, and he occasionally joins a Sunday gospel choir. Music is a big part of his life; he follows hip‑hop, R&B, and local indie bands, and he attends live performances at venues around Indianapolis. He also likes cooking soul‑food dishes that remind him of family gatherings. To manage his anxiety, Lorenzo practices guided meditation, keeps a reflective journal, and attends a weekly support group for men dealing with stress. He is an avid fan of the Indianapolis Colts and enjoys watching games with friends. Additionally, he volunteers at a neighborhood youth program, helping teenagers with homework and mentoring them on time‑management skills.
info.sports_persona: Lorenzo Kelley stays active by playing pickup basketball at the local community center and competing in a weekend league with the Indianapolis Parks Basketball Association, maintains fitness with regular cardio sessions, and follows the Indianapolis Colts, Indiana Pacers, and Indianapolis Indians, though they sometimes skip a workout when anxiety spikes.
info.arts_persona: Lorenzo Kelley sings in a Sunday gospel choir, follows hip‑hop and R&B icons like Kendrick Lamar and H.E.R., supports the local indie band The Hoosier Echoes, and regularly attends live shows at The Hi‑Fi, where the blend of music fuels their creative spirit.
info.travel_persona: Lorenzo Kelley prefers short road‑trip getaways that fit their variable schedule, enjoys weekend escapes to Nashville for its music scene, Chicago for its architecture, and the Indiana Dunes for outdoor relaxation, and dreams of a cultural immersion trip to New Orleans to explore its cuisine and jazz heritage.
info.culinary_persona: Lorenzo Kelley delights in cooking soul‑food classics such as fried catfish, collard greens, cornbread, and sweet‑potato casserole, boasts a solid home‑cooking skill level, often experiments with spice blends, but has a habit of over‑indulging in fried dishes during weekend gatherings.
